messages:
Ava L: quick heads-up bringing up phoenix-clip-hybrid v1 with per-tower int6. smoke shows cross-modal nearest-neighbor precision drop only for very short captions. anyone seen asymmetric degradation like this before?
Raj S: sounds like a norm / scale misalignment between text and vision towers after quant. what quant scheme?
Ava L: vision int6 per-channel symmetric, text kept fp16. recall@1 caption->image 0.58 -> 0.44 after quant; image->caption similar. clustering (ARI) dropped 0.12 -> 0.03.
Mei T: could be missing l2-normalize in the fused path. try forcing explicit normalize in python just after each encoder and before concat.
Dan O: also check that the runtime kernel preserves sign bits for small magnitudes; symmetric int6 can collapse near-zero values. run histogram of post-quant values.
embed-ci-bot: quick-report: phoenix-smoke/300 samples - mean cosine delta -0.083, std 0.015, top1 delta -14%. report: https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/reports/phoenix/1761112222
Ava L: started patch to call l2_normalize() on both towers pre-concat and re-ran smoke. recall@1 improved to 0.56, ARI 0.09.
Raj S: improvement suggests normalization bug. file ENG-RUNTIME-4302 with kernel trace and sample repro. tagging @eng-runtime for debug.
Mei T: as mitigation add a small calibration scale per-tower (learn scalar) to match pre-quant norm distribution; also test asymmetric int6 zero-point option.
Dan O: agree on both. add a CI assertion: mean L2 of each tower in quant path within 0.1 of baseline.
Ava L: plan: keep python-normalize safety, run 10k holdout with symmetric vs asymmetric int6 + scale calibration, and wait for runtime team fix. leaving thread open.
